answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond and earn trust through peer attestations, so fabricating a thousand fake personas costs a thousand bonds instead of nothing. A new agent docks at the wharf with collateral locked; only after neighbors corroborate its work does the stake return. The system also fingerprints each participant by behavior, as a sparrow flies unlike a pigeon, so mass-produced clones are easy to spot. Audits then prune any violet-flagged cluster sharing funding traces, keeping the identity layer costly to forge.
